owner: CC owns the validate machine's code and proofs (cairn/devices/builder/machines/validate/). The exit-gate ordering itself — verdict complete-and-passing BEFORE the PROVED crossing — is ruled physics (ticket proved-answers-the-chart) and is not the part in question; the defect is upstream, in what the brick lets a criterion demand.
intention: A validate criterion is runnable at the moment the exit gate demands its verdict: every instrument a criterion names reads state that exists BEFORE the PROVED crossing, so the verdict artifact the gate shape-checks is measurement, never a promise about the crossing it is supposed to precede.
why: MEASURED 2026-08-15, on the first voyage to close through both gates end-to-end (the-present-tense-corpus-rewrites-once). The claiming validate berth's criteria 3 and 4 each embedded a post-PROVED observation: criterion 3 demanded 'the compiler's history carries this ticket's BUILDME, PROVEME and PROVED crossings' — the PROVED entry cannot exist when the verdict must be complete, because the verdict is the PROVED crossing's own entry condition (ExitGateRed otherwise); criterion 4 demanded the parent probe's _cleanup_landed() return True, and that predicate flips on the ticket cursor writing [PROVED], which happens after the crossing. The builder resolved it by measuring everything measurable pre-crossing, recording the ordering defect as a named falsification in the verdict's evidence, and re-measuring live after the cursor write — an honest workaround, which is exactly what a defect looks like the day before it is physics. The brick's judges (validate-filters: VALIDATE_MEASURES_DONE, VALIDATE_COVERS_THE_BUILD) check that a criterion carries an instrument and covers the pieces; nothing checks WHEN the instrument can run. A criterion that can only be satisfied after the crossing is a verdict deferred past the gate that reads it — the gate then either refuses a true build or passes a narrated one.
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. A criterion whose instrument cannot run yet yields a verdict that is a hypothesis wearing a measurement's fields.

Law 4 — the exit-gate ordering is physics (proved-answers-the-chart); a criterion the ordering makes unrunnable is the schema contradicting its own gate, and the fix belongs in the schema, not in each voyage's workaround.
gates: The validate brick's door and the build_inspector's judges (one implementation, two mouths — the chart-validate pattern). The natural home is a third judge beside VALIDATE_MEASURES_DONE: a criterion whose instrument names the ticket's own PROVED state, the exit gate's own artifacts, or a predicate documented to flip at the cursor write, is refused at the door with the offending criterion named.
falsifier: DONE when the validate door refuses a packet carrying a criterion that reads post-crossing state (proved by refiring the two defective criteria from verdict-20260815T150437-70306f8bfca3's source berth verbatim and watching them refuse), while the same packet with pre-crossing criteria passes. WRONG INTENT if a legitimate class of post-crossing criterion exists that the chart must be able to express — in which case the answer is a labeled after-the-crossing field the exit gate knows to defer, never an unlabeled criterion the builder discovers is unrunnable at the close.
horizon: One voyage: the judge is small (a predicate over the criterion's instrument text and the chain's ticket), the evidence criteria are already on disk, and the door/judge composition pattern is settled by validate-filters.
dependencies: validate-filters (the judges this adds a sibling to)
distinctions_recorded: the defect is in the brick, not the gate: the exit gate behaved exactly as ruled; what failed is that the chart authored a done-condition the ruled ordering makes unobservable at judgment time

the workaround on record (measure pre-crossing, name the falsification, re-measure post-write) is the manual protocol until this lands — a voyage hitting the same shape should cite this ticket rather than re-derive it

SIBLING TICKET, AND THE LINE BETWEEN THEM: an-instrument-that-cannot-bite-is-refused-at-the-verdict (cast 2026-08-17) holds the same field for a different failure. This ticket is TIME — the instrument reads state that does not exist yet, so it cannot RUN when the exit gate demands its verdict, and a text predicate over the instrument string can catch it at validate's door. That one is CAPABILITY — the instrument runs, at the right moment, against real state, and cannot tell pass from fail. Measured there at n=3 in one voyage (staleness-is-about-this-process-not-about-disk, 2026-08-17): a grep whose 16 hits came from the module's own explanatory prose, a revert that could not red because the fixture injects the answer, and a git stash that made the tooth ERROR at import rather than FAIL by name. Neither fix reaches the other's defect, which is why they were not merged: a text predicate cannot see capability (it is a fact about the tree, not about the sentence), and running an instrument earlier says nothing about whether it discriminates. If both land, they are two clauses in the same refusal and should be proved together.

THE WATCH THAT MATTERS HERE IS A LIVE REFUSAL, NOT A FIXTURE ONE, and the proof cannot supply it. The falsifier fires the judge at two criteria pulled from verdict-20260815T150437-70306f8bfca3 — an artifact already known to be defective — so a green there says only that the judge CAN bite something pre-selected for biting. Whether it bites what builders actually WRITE is a different question with a different population, answerable only against live packets. That gap is why this ticket carries a watch at all rather than resting on its proof, and the watch's `enough` refuses to close until one REAL packet has been refused.

provenance: Measured 2026-08-15 at the step-6 close of the-present-tense-corpus-rewrites-once: the verdict artifact verdict-20260815T150437-70306f8bfca3 records the falsification in its evidence, and the voyage's slate (2026-08-15-the-sweep-lands-the-corpus-is-one-tense) carries it in open_threads. intent_berth: none, because this is a bug: the validate brick admits a criterion its own downstream gate makes unrunnable, and editing the brick's judges fixes it (ruling 2026-08-02, three entry points). No new intention is being born — chart-validate already intends 'done is verified in the world by the instrument', and an instrument that cannot run yet fails that intention as surely as a missing one.

watchme.trigger: every firing of the validate door — the door is the sole path to a validate berth, so the firing IS the event and nothing polls. The probe reads the judged packet and records whether the time-judge fired, on which criterion, and whether the packet was one a builder was about to berth
watchme.enough: when the door has judged thirty validate packets AND at least one REAL packet — one a builder authored for a live voyage, not a fixture — has been refused by this judge. The refusal on live work is the whole measurement: the proof shows the judge CAN bite a fixture, and only a live refusal shows it bites what people actually write. Stop early and loudly on either falsifying observation: a criterion refused that a reader judges legitimate (the WRONG INTENT clause arriving — the answer is the labeled deferred field, not a weaker judge), or a voyage that reaches the exit gate and works around an unrunnable criterion by hand, which is the original defect walking past its own judge
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier: per firing, whether the time-judge fired, the criterion text and its named instrument, whether the packet was fixture or live, and the disposition — refused, passed, or worked-around-at-the-close
watchme.nexus: the validate brick's own tree, because the question is about what builders write into criteria and the tree is what teaches the next criterion its shape
watchme.consumer: the builder authoring the next validate packet, who pays for an unrunnable criterion at the close; and the exit gate, which currently absorbs the defect as a narrated verdict
